title: A board git moved after the store recorded it takes the store's older render on the next write, because 0614's guard spares a board only when the file index holds NO record
body:
## What

A board that git moved after the store recorded it takes the store's older render on the next write. 0614's guard (8f1fda69b, vc's ruling (c')) leaves a board only when its `board.json` differs from the store's render AND the file index holds no record of it. A 3.2.5+ warm records every board, so once a store exists the guard never fires. When a checkout, a reset or a merge moves the board files forward under that store, the next write that renders boards puts the store's older content over every newer file, and nothing names it.

## Repro (dc, 2026-10-23, measured)

In a scratch clone of main, with hooks off, a short isolated HOME, XDG empty and no daemon:

1. `git checkout --detach b5e0fd2b3`, then warm a store (`intent wb status`). The store's cc board holds heartbeat 2026-10-23T18:27:25.410Z.
2. `git checkout --detach 93a41a24b`. The committed board files move forward (cc's heartbeat is 19:50:05.166Z there) and the store does not.
3. Make any edit to `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/gen_dispatch_table.sh`, so the sync has a difference to carry, then run `intent sync --to-store ST0056`.

The sync replaces ST0056 as asked. It also rewrites the `board.json` and `wip.md` of every node whose board changed between the two commits (cc, dc, ic and vc) with b5e0fd2b3's content. cc's `wip.md` goes from `heartbeat_at: 2026-10-23 19:50Z` to `18:27Z`, and its focus back to the line before its fold. Nothing on stderr names a board. The rewritten files equal b5e0fd2b3's committed boards byte for byte.

Both binaries do it, byte-identically: the installed pair (`intent 3.2.5 (c59e807790f3...) dev`) and cc's combined build of 0630's banks (`dirty-0f445065b`, tree 22ee4a0387a6). So this is 0614's class, not 0630's.

The controls: with no store before the sync (a cold store the sync itself creates) at 93a41a24b, neither binary writes any board, with the tool edit or without it. The cold warm reads the current files, and in both binaries every board then has a file-index row.

The script is `refs/bank/dc/dc3/stale-store-repro.sh` (blob 464ce86ab542), taking `<src-checkout> <bin-dir> <short scratch>`. Its run with the installed pair is `refs/bank/dc/dc3/repro-installed.log` (blob 709b6d9308dd).

## How it was found

It was found in cc's stack-judging worktree, `tmp/wt-cc-0616t`. That worktree was checked out at 18:28Z on 2026-10-23, then moved by `git reset` to four later commits under the same store. A scoped `intent sync --to-store ST0056` there rewrote every node's board backwards. The first reading blamed 0630's fix-s4 (a scan row for every view on first sight), and the measurement above refutes it (vc's ORDER dc-3).

## The class

- 0614's Expected, "A sync inside a linked worktree never writes a view older than the commit the worktree stands on", is met only for a store that an Intent before 3.2.5 warmed.
- It bites any worktree whose HEAD moves under an existing store, which a stack judge does by design, and any checkout whose board files move while the store holds the older state.

## Where it is (read, not measured)

- `Facade::sync_from_disk`, the `--to-store` restore, lands its projection with `WriteSet::commit` and never passes through `land_board_write`, so 0614's guard is not on this path at all.
- `Facade::projection` puts one board file per node in every projection, "not narrowed by a thread scope". So a scoped restore renders every board from the store, and in the repro that store's boards were older than the files.
- The store already asks the provenance question for boards elsewhere. `carry_pulled_boards` (`sync --apply`) takes a board only when the store's render still hashes to the recorded bytes and the file moved forward. The unscoped resync keeps the previous row for a board ahead of the store rather than marking it seen. The fix asks the same question, not a second one.

## Spec (vc, 2026-10-23)

- The guard's condition becomes: the file's bytes differ from the row the store last recorded for it (a row whose sha256 is not the file's, or no row). Such a board is left as it is and named on stderr with the `intent sync --to-store` remedy, exactly as 0614's no-record case is.
- The arm is this repro as a Rust arm beside 0614's `a_board_write_leaves_a_board_nothing_records.rs`. A second arm is a variant where a full scan runs between the checkout and the write, so that a rescanned row cannot read as "nobody moved it".

## Raised by

dc (intent-dc), on vc's ORDER dc-4, from cc's observation, measured in dc's ORDER dc-3.


## The judged run (2026-10-24), and the ruling: 3.2.7

dc's fix was banked as `refs/bank/dc/0635/fix` (blob e5799abfb283, patch-id 70d5baeaa641) and judged by one stacked run, `refs/bank/dc/0635/run.sh`, on hv's "Go", in `tmp/wt-dc-0635` at tree T3 06e3559019f7, which is main's HEAD 29c658790 plus the bank on every code path. The bank stays on that ref for 3.2.7, unlanded.

THE RED, the bank's own arm: `a_board_git_moved_under_the_store_is_left::a_full_scan_between_the_checkout_and_the_write_does_not_read_a_moved_board_as_unmoved` panicked at the test file's line 126:20 with `bb's own write: WbBoardsNotInTheStore { nodes: ["aa"] }`. After two full ingest passes over the moved board and the scoped restore, bb's own board write refused rather than leaving aa's board and naming it. The intentsvcs suite stood at 1689 passed, 1 failed, 4 ignored; every other test binary was green, and so were fmt, both clippy lines and doc. The control behaved as predicted: with the bank's intentsvcs hunks reversed, both arms failed at their assertions, with no compile error. The shell half was stopped on vc's order once the red was in, so it gave no verdict.

The run's stamps, whole (UTC):

THE RULING (hv's, before the run: one stacked run, 3.2.7 on a red, no second try; vc's attribution of 2026-10-23 21:55Z, a red in an arm that exercises what the bank changes counts against it): 0635 drops to 3.2.7 whole and stays OPEN. hv can override.
